utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you and good morning, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Judge Moloto is for reasons of authorised Tribunal business is unable to continue to sit for a period which is likely to be of short duration, and Judge Fluegge and myself are satisfied that it's in the interest of justice to continue to hear the case in the absence of Judge Moloto. And since we expect that it will not be for a period of longer than five working days, we decided that we'll proceed under Rule 15 bis. Are there any preliminary matters? I am not informed of any. Therefore, we are at a point where the Defence is invited to call its next witness, a witness to be called by videolink. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. The Defence at this time would call Milosav Gagovic via videolink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's then first establish whether the videolink is functioning.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] We can hear you and we can see you and witness just entered the videolink room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you inform us who else are in the videolink room?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Apart from myself and the witness, there is one ITSS official.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar, for that. Good morning, Witness, Mr. Gagovic, I presume. I see that you are now putting on your earphones. Good morning, Mr. Gagovic, I presume.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [via videolink] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gagovic, before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration. The text will be handed out to you. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [via videolink] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gagovic. Please be seated. Mr. Gagovic, you'll first be examined by Mr. Ivetic. Mr. Ivetic is a member of Mr. Mladic's Defence team. Mr. Ivetic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Colonel. Can you please state your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning. I'm a retired colonel. My name is Milosav Gagovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would ask that you be shown 1D4121, a witness statement from the Karadzic proceedings.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [via videolink] It's quite small. The letters are small. I cannot see anything. But the document is in front of me, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Then I'm waiting for the same to come up on e-court on this end. If we could please turn to the last page in the Serbian language.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I would direct your attention to the signature at the bottom of the page, and I would ask if you could identify for us whose signature we see there.

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And subsequent to signing this statement for the Karadzic case, did you have occasion to review the same in the Serbian language to ascertain if everything is correct therein?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: I have just looked at it. I've read it and signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you stand by everything as contained in your written statement as being accurate?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, if I were to ask you today questions about the same topics as contained in your written statement, would the answers that you would give today be in essence the same as in the statement?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And given that you have taken a solemn declaration to tell the truth, would those answers as contained in the statement be truthful in nature?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender the statement 1D4121 into evidence at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, the statement would receive number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit D622, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence in the absence of any objections. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, we also have three associated exhibits that as of yet are not in evidence out of the five that are mentioned in the statement. However, since the statement is from the Karadzic case, it has 65 ter numbers from that case. So I wanted to seek Your Honour's guidance as to how we should memorialise the corresponding Mladic numbers. I would suggest, perhaps, filing a chart as an additional exhibit listing both sets of numbers and then advising the parties and the Registrar of the number of that document once it's in e-court, if that's Your Honour's preference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Filing a chart, and I take it from Ms. Bibles nodding that she agrees, that it would be an appropriate solution.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: That's correcting Your Honour. A table of concordance, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Table of concordance to be filed by the Defence, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I will do that and then I will advise Your Honours accordingly of the identification number for that document. At this time I would like to read are a brief summary of the witness's statement which has been explained to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Between 1988 and 1992, Colonel Gagovic was the assistant for logistics in the JNA 4th Corps in Sarajevo. From 10 May 1992 to 1 June 1992, he was the acting commander of the JNA 4th Corps in Sarajevo. His testimony is that the SDA headed by Alija Izetbegovic seemed to follow the goals publicly promulgated by Izetbegovic; namely, that an Islamic state could be created in Bosnia-Herzegovina, whereas the SDS and Dr. Karadzic wanted all the constitutive people of Bosnia-Herzegovina to be created equality. Already in 1990 and 1991, the 4th Corps received information about SDA and HDZ paramilitaries being formed in Bosnia-Herzegovina. The referendum on independence was presented by Izetbegovic to the JNA as really being a move to strengthen his personal bargaining position with the other republican presidents rather than for independence. After said referendum, a witch hunt started against Serbs in Sarajevo. Various Serbs were killed and families received threats to leave their apartment or be killed. A paramilitary commanded by Sefer Halilovic made up of Muslims from the Sandzak region in Serbia attacked Ilidza in April 1992 from Sokolovic Colony. The BiH presidency asked for the JNA to intervene and send a unit to this area. However, when the JNA complied, the crew of a JNA transporter was taken captive and killed by the Muslim forces. After the JNA was blockaded in its barracks, the Muslim forces attacked the airport. The HJNA reached an agreement with Alija Izetbegovic, witnessed by General MacKenzie and Colm Doyle, for a peaceful withdrawal of the JNA from Sarajevo. However, the Muslim side attacked the convoy and reneged on the agreement killing five JNA colonels, eight military policemen, and one Muslim civilian female serving in the JNA, while wounding and taking captive others. Those taken captive were beaten at the Partizan Sports Complex. The witness knows of several documents issued by the Muslim leadership in Sarajevo instructing that JNA convoys be attacked. The witness states that the JNA was not working on a division of Sarajevo. And that completes the summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivetic. If you have any additional questions you may put them to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Colonel, I do have some more questions. If we could first look at paragraph 11, which is on page 3 of the English and page 5 of the Serbian in your statement. Here you talk of a witch hunt against Serbs in Sarajevo following the Bosnian referendum. Who were the perpetrators of these various incidents and killings that you have described in this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Those who played a main role in the killings that I mentioned in this paragraph were, up until that time, paramilitary forces of the Muslims. And they were supported, in my opinion, by the legal leadership.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note, we can hardly hear the witness. The interpreters are not able to hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. Could the witness come closer to the microphones because the interpreters have difficulties in hearing him, and could we restart. Is it -- could you say a few words, Witness, so we can check whether the interpreters are now able to hear you? Are there any problems as far as the interpretation is concerned?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it seems that when the witness began the volume was loud and then it's suddenly so low we can hardly hear him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That seems to be a technical problem because I also hear -- when the witness starts speaking I hear him clearly. And then -- is it -- could you speak another few words, Mr. Gagovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [via videolink] Let me continue now. The first incident was the killing of the father of the bridegroom Nikola Gadovic and the priest was also killed, the one who was supposed to perform the marriage of the bride and groom. After that, sportsmen were attacked. There was a person who was in the Bosnia-Herzegovina martial arts team and he was supposed to take part in a demonstration for the independence of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Then there were the two Trifkovic brothers. One of them was crucified on the Jewish cemetery like Christ as one could say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I stop you there. You're repeating what we find already in the statement. The question was: Who were responsible for those incidents? Rather than to repeat to describe them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [via videolink] All right. I don't know how much of this information you have. The legal and the legitimate authorities of the city of Sarajevo and of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina were responsible because it's normal that the organs that the people elected would be responsible for everything that goes on in a republic. And this was carried out by members of the paramilitary forces and the police forces that were then made up by -- made up of Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, perhaps the source of knowledge and the identification of perpetrators might need some further attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, could you please tell the Court what is the bases of your knowledge of the perpetrators of these incidents in paragraph 11 in your statement?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Based on information that was available during that time and through the television and from other information, the daily newspapers, and, of course, on the basis of everything that happened, the corpses and the victims that were being buried in Sarajevo during that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles, is there any dispute about these incidents having taken place?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Or do you challenge --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: -- in terms -- in terms of the events themselves, obviously there has been testimony about this. We don't -- there may be -- there is dispute, perhaps, about the details. But in terms of the events having taken place and been newsworthy, certainly not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the Prosecution does not challenge that if an attack on a Serbia wedding party taken place, that it would not have been Serbs who attacked that wedding party. Is that -- without saying, then, who exactly was responsible.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would have to defer. I would have to do some checking before I could agree to that on the record. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But there is no challenge at this moment in this respect. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could now move --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it may be clear that if this is part of the statement where perpetrators are mentioned, that it comes as a bit of a surprise that the witness learned it from television and from the media because then we'd rather have a look at the media and find out what was published about the events at the time, the events in itself not being in dispute. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can move to paragraph 31 through 32 of your written statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's in page 11 of the Serbian and page 7 and 8 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Here, sir, you are describing the situation revolving around the Faletici weapons depot. Can you please provide for details about whom attacked whom and how the Serb TO got involved in this incident?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: The weapons depot in Faletici was guarded by members of the Yugoslav Peoples' Army. The attack was carried out by the paramilitary forces of the Muslims. There was a conflict between the security and the attackers. There was a TO company in the immediate vicinity of the Serbian municipality of Pale, because the depot was halfway between Pale and Sarajevo. The company went to protect the security of the depot. The Muslim forces pulled back. According to the data that was available to us, there were no dead or wounded on either side. The Serb forces then managed to get their hands on the equipment and weaponry that was in the Faletici depot. The presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina intervened with the command of the 2nd Military District requesting that they be given two-thirds of the weaponry because allegedly, according to the population structure, the ratio between the Serbs, Muslims, and Croats, that was proportion that was due to them. The JNA didn't have the opportunity to take back the weapons, and so the General Staff decided to bring a certain amount of requested weaponry from the Pancevo depot. This was light infantry weaponry. In agreement with the B and H presidency and the UNPROFOR command, the weapons were to be shipped to the facility where UNPROFOR was. This was the former PTT engineering building in Sarajevo and that it should not be handed either to the population nor to the paramilitary forces directly. However, when the first trailer-trucks arrived with the weapons and crossed into the territory being covered by the Muslim paramilitary forces, the trailer-trucks were stopped and the weapons were looted and taken from the vehicles. The other vehicles were stopped and so there were no more weapons shipments.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Just to clarify one aspect. You mentioned Pancevo. Where is Pancevo located?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Pancevo is in the immediate vicinity of Belgrade in the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I put a question to the witness, in the meantime. I would like to know how you, Mr. Gagovic, learned about all of that, what you told us just a minute ago? What is the source of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [via videolink] I was assistant commander for logistics at the time, and the assets and vehicles went through Lukavica, where I was billeted, together with my organs. We exerted our influence for the assets to arrive to the PTT engineering building. We secured their passage until we reached the territory controlled by the paramilitary Muslim forces. I think it was close to the Nedzarici line in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, Colonel, were all weapons depots guarded by the JNA or with were there also depots guarded by other entities?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: In Sarajevo and it's environs, there were depots secured by organs of the TO. They were the depots of smaller units, territorial companies and battalions. There was also a depot in Busovaca which belonged to the JNA, however it was guarded by the Croatian TO bodies; that is to say, Bosnian Croats, those who resided in Bosnia that did not come from Croatia. Unfortunately, there was a clash at that depot between the Croatian guards and Muslim bodies who came to take the part of weapons they believed belonged to them. Eleven Muslim members were killed on the occasion. Alija Izetbegovic, the president of the presidency, personally engaged in -- was personally engaged in dealing with the problem, together with Franjo Boras and Mr. Boban. There was a danger of further escalation between the Muslim and Croatian population. They came up with a solution that I'm not aware of. In any case, the event that took place at the Busovaca depot was never publicised. It never went public.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, in relation to those depots -- weapons depots that were guarded by the JNA, what were the standing orders from the JNA General Staff? Were they supposed to give those weapons to any of the sides in the Bosnian conflict?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: The General Staff order was that no one was to be issued with those weapons without prior approval. In agreement with the TO command of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the weapons could only be distributed as part of that entity. As for immediate use - that is to say, the weapons that had been previously used to train the TO of Bosnia-Herzegovina - the order could have been issued by the zone staff commander, the TO zone staff, that is. I believe that some time in September 1991 that right was revoked and the most senior officer who could issue orders to have their weapons issued for purposes of TO training became the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to turn to paragraph 35 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: To be found on page 8 in English, page 12 in the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, here you are discussing a document that changed the name of some of the JNA 4th Corps units. I'd like to direct your attention to the document P4443 and would first ask you if this is, in fact, the same document at issue?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the document before me is the one you referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, during the Dragomir Milosevic trial --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have a look at P4443 --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Oh, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, during the Dragomir Milosevic trial you are recorded at transcript page 8701 as not recognising this document and saying that you cannot exclude it perhaps being a fake. Can you please explain for us your current position as to the authenticity of this document?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: When I testified in the Milosevic case and when I was shown this document, I asserted at the time, as I do now, that the signature on this document is mine. I was then asked whether this document could be a counterfeit, and I did say that I could not exclude that possibility. However, I really could not recall why I would have signed this document. Later on I consulted the drafter of the document. He confirmed as follows: The order referred to in this order issued by the command of the 2nd Military District, although I cannot read it now because it is too small, was the one that this is -- was based on. Since many units of the 4th JNA Corps were manned by military recruits, soldiers and officers from Bosnia-Herzegovina - that is to say, Bosnian Serbs, Muslims, and a small number of Croats - as of the 4th of May, the 4th Corps was ordered to have all FRY citizens should be moved back to Yugoslavia. And it was then decided that the 4th Corps would become the Sarajevo Romanija Corps. Given the fact that they knew how many of their members were FRY citizens in the 4th Corps, they decided to rely on BH citizens to form the nucleus of those units. Some units were established anew as well. The military district command on General Staff orders decided not to use the establishment names when forming the units of the 4th Corps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. Mr. Ivetic, you were asking about why the witness now considers -- would exclude that it's a fake. Is there any dispute about this being a -- not a fake document but an authentic document?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Certainly the position of the Prosecution is that it is an authentic document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: He has previously disputed that fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Why do we have to -- if that was a mistake in the past, why do we have to explore exactly why that was a mistake by the witness where he now says that it's an authentic document. And apart from that, he's going into all kind of details which certainly are not part of the question, Mr. Ivetic. If you're interested in them, then please put a focused question to the witness so that he can answer that one instead of for minutes and minutes to explain the background of why the 4th Corps was changed by name and please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. But I would stress that we have a discrepancy that we explored with the witness and which the witness is explaining. I hope that Your Honours are not saying that that is an improper procedure to do with the witness, to discuss discrepancies in prior testimony, because I think that's precisely what we are supposed to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. But as a matter of fact, the present testimony is not contested and you are supporting that as well. There is no -- unless the Prosecution would later on in cross-examination start discrediting the witness because he did not exclude for a possibility in the past. Is that your intention, Ms. Bibles?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think his testimony in the Dragomir Milosevic case was actually much stronger than excluding the possibility that it was a forgery. We may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: -- pursue that in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. If that's the case, then you could also leave it for re-examination, but -- Mr. Ivetic, there seems to be no dispute about the accuracy of the -- what the witness tells us now. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. If we can then return to the witness statement which is now marked D622, and if we could go to page 2 in English -- and the bottom of page 2 and top of page 3 in the Serbian, paragraph 5 of the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The bottom of page 2 is redacted, Mr. Ivetic. I had a similar --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Top --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- in the [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's on the bottom of page 2 in the B/C/S. In the English, paragraph 5 is the top of page 2 just above the reaction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Paragraph number is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 5. Because elsewhere in the statement we find a reference to paragraph 6. Paragraph is 6 --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- redacted as well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, in -- sir --

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- in paragraph -- in paragraph 5 --

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, in paragraph 5 you mention a document from the JNA --

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: There is no tone in my headset.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, in this paragraph, you mention a document from JNA security organs about the SDA paramilitaries. I would like to show you 1D4202.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we can also call it up in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The first question I would have is: Is this the document that is referenced in this paragraph of your statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, this number is included and mentioned in the Karadzic statement. Is this the right statement in our case?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise. You're correct, Your Honours. It's 1D4122 in our case.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, the question I have for you is: Is this the same document that is discussed in paragraph 5 of your statement?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the contents are the same. But this one seems to have been copied several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, this document talks of Muslim JNA members participating in meetings of these SDA paramilitaries. What action did the JNA take against its members identified as participating in the Bosnian Muslim paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: They were not sanctioned. There were no measures applied, save for interviews which took place with those officers. It was put to them that they may face consequences resulting from different events should Bosnia-Herzegovina problems be -- continue being dealt with in this way, through political leadership. The work of those officers was monitored by security organs, the very ones submitted this report. When certain officers sensed that they were being monitored, some of them did not wish to change their course of action and left the JNA units. They joined the side they believed to be theirs. As far as I know, not one of them was sanctioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, could you guide the Chamber where we find exactly the events or the incidents you were referring to in your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. If we can turn to the last page in both languages of the document that's up on the screen, we will see a discussion of a captain, I believe, Sakib Mahmutovic. On the English at the top, we also have 2nd Lieutenant Safet Bejtovic. If we go to the prior page in English we have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But let me see. Let me try to understand it. Mahmutovic is described as a potential supporter at a meeting of a group I'm not yet aware of. I mean, this document is new for the Chamber, so therefore if you could take us with the witness through the document in such a way that we understand his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, could you please tell the Chamber what kind of information was reported to the JNA 4th Corps collegium by way of this report and others like it submitted during the relevant time-period?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: I was a member of the corps commanders collegium as was the chief of intelligence, Lieutenant-Colonel Simovic at the time. The collegium of the corps commander was regularly briefed on the contents of such documents. They involved events in the field and the activities of certain political parties vis-à-vis the JNA and amongst themselves as well as their communication with their ethnic community and the other communities. The information flow continued in 1991 when the chief of security at the corps command was Lieutenant-Colonel Fikret Muslimovic. Upon his departure for the national defence school, he was replaced by the former desk officer of the department, Colonel -- actually, Lieutenant-Colonel --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, there seems to be a great misunderstanding. Your question was: "Now, this document talks of Muslim JNA members participating in meetings of these SDA paramilitaries." The only thing I'm trying to understand is where do I find this in this document so that I know what the witness is talking about. Witness, could you assist us in where exactly in this four-page document where Muslim JNA members participating in meetings with SDA paramilitary is to be found?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, perhaps there is a misunderstanding. Every paragraph on every page discusses that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [via videolink] You have the names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then perhaps we should read -- let me see. Well, I'm unable to immediately identify in a four-page document whether this is the gist of the -- the gist of the document, but I'll ask for a copy to be printed out and have a look at it at the next break. Then please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Colonel, do you know why it was that the JNA did not take any more stringent disciplinary action against its members and former members who participated in such meetings?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Because it was the position of the General Staff that the JNA, as the military organisation, should not get involved in any political matters in the field. As for the officers themselves, they had the right to be affiliated with a political party. By the same token, the institutions of the corps command were under an obligation to conduct interviews with those officers trying to indicate to them that they took a wrong turn along the way. At the time, it was seen as a political affiliation or a political opinion. By that time, no political party was openly against the JNA or the joint state. At least according to the statements they were making at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to move to my final area of questioning on paragraph 40 of your statement, the last page in both languages. Again, your statement being D622. And, sir, in paragraph 40, you talk of a twisted image as to the number and distribution of heavy weapons in Sarajevo. Could you please detail for us what is the twisted image you speak of and what was the true facts on the ground as to the heavy weapons number and distribution in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: The image was twisted not only in terms of the number of assets as well as many other pieces of information that was presented at the time. When it comes to artillery assets in the possession of both the Serb and Muslim side, especially on the Serbian side, the numbers were inflated even ten-fold. So in the media, one could see notices to citizens that there are 500-plus artillery pieces deployed around Sarajevo as well as rocket systems and so on and so forth. However, the corps had the following assets of 120-, 130-millimetres as well as 150-millimetres. We had a total of 54 artillery pieces including four rocket systems of 128-millimetre calibre. On the Muslim side, some 34 artillery pieces were left behind including a multiple rocket launcher of 128-millimetre calibre. The media presented to the public that one side had several hundred pieces, whereas the other side basic had none. They said that no weapons were left on the other side that used to belong to the JNA and the training centre in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. That question concludes my direct examination. I thank you, Colonel, for your evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [via videolink] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I had a glance through the document. I tried to do it very quickly, Mr. Ivetic. It seems that there is two specific versions are mentioned, one apparently retired JNA officer. The other one a bit mysterious whether Mr. Imamovic was retired or was not retired. That's what I could make up.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And then on the list page, a Second Lieutenant Safet Bijetovic and a Captain Sakib Mahmutovic that I referenced during the direct examination when I first called this document up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Indicative information that was supposedly in contact with their man at the MUP BH. Yes. There are certainly reasons for the reporter to believe that there are links.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, are you tendering this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It is an associated exhibit and so it was going to be one of the ones that I was going to prepare a chart of concordance for. There are three that are not in evidence of the five that are identified in the Karadzic case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, talking about a chart of concordance, I think that in your annex B to the motion that already the numbers in both the Karadzic case and in the Mladic case appear next to each other, so there seems to be already on the record some kind of a chart of concordance.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There is that. That's why I asked for Your Honour's guidance as to whether we need to do another one as an exhibit or whether we can rely on what's been filed with the 92 ter. I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we can rely on what has been filed for the 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Especially since --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- we have now paid specific attention to where to find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you then, Your Honour. In that case I would also tender 65 ter numbers 1D --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I just take the time to -- okay. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: 65 ter numbers 1D04122.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That is the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The document we just looked at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just have a look. Yes, the one signed by Simovic. No objections, Ms. Bibles. Perhaps we go through the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the list and see whether there are any objections. And if not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The next one would be 1D03108.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear no objections. Next one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That would be the only three that need to be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The other two have already been admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, 1D040122 would receive number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D623, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. 1D03108 would receive?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D624, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted. 1D00176 would receive number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D625.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. We are at a point of having a break. Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [via videolink] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- we'll take a break of 20 minutes. We'd like to see you back after 20 minutes when cross-examination will be conducted by Ms. Bibles. We resume at 10 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we just establish whether the videolink is still functional?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, I don't hear Madam Registrar at the far end and I see an indication on my screen that the microphone is switched off. But it's now on again.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, I hereby confirm that we can hear you and we can see you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we can proceed. Mr. Gagovic, you'll now be cross-examined by Ms. Bibles. Ms. Bibles is counsel for the Prosecution. Ms. Bibles, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, from your statement, we understand that your role as acting commander for the JNA 4th Corps ended on 1 June 1992. Did you physically leave Sarajevo after that date?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was not an acting commander but representing the commander. So that's a little bit more of a milder function. But, yes, after that I did leave.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you for the clarification. Is it true that you retired shortly after this time-period?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was placed on the retirement list already in April because I met all the conditions. But since there was a change, practically the JNA ceased to exist, then once I came to Sarajevo I went to visit my family, and then on the 6th of June I submitted my request for retirement. I was --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: -- approved a leave of three months but I had left before my retirement was due. You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to direct your attention to the 10th and 11th of May 1992. You were at Lukavica on that date?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: During these dates, did General Mladic come to Lukavica to tell you and others that he had assumed the duties of the commander of the 2nd Military District?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, General Mladic came to Lukavica on the 10th of May with General Kukanjac who was the commander of the 2nd Military District before him, and they said that there would be a switch, and they said that Mladic was appointed acting commander of the 2nd Military District.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And, sir, I believe you previously testified that General Mladic went from unit to unit to get to know people under his command. My question for you is whether General, is it Baros, B-a-r-o-s, was included in that list that he communicated with during that time period?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: General Baros did not actually belong to the 2nd Military District command. He was the director of the training centre that was directly subordinated to the infantry of the General Staff. However, since he was in the area of responsibility of the 2nd Military District of the JNA and the barracks were blocked, then General Mladic was contacting him. I was also in touch with him as a representative of the corps commander, as well as certain organs of the UNPROFOR and the European community.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And, sir, was General Baros available over the telephone and radio?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: General Baros did not have telephone. He communicated via radio.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could have P2728, which is an 11 May 1992 intercept, the transcripts brought to our screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, you're aware from previous testimony that some conversations of yours were intercepted including one on the 11th of May 1992 between yourself, General Mladic, and General Baros. Is that -- does that accurately depict your knowledge about this conversation?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did have conversations with General Baros. Practically, I was his main link with the world outside of the barracks because he didn't have any other means to communicate other than via radio, and then I would passes on information by telephone because I was the only one who had the telephone number. So I was his link with the command and the barracks. Others didn't have telephones, so you will get the impression that everything was actually being done over that one telephone that happened to be in my office.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And, sir, that explains why there are a number of intercepted communications with your voice on them?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And if we could turn now to page 3 in both languages. And I'd like to focus about a third of the way down in English. I think it's close to that in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, during this conversation, General Mladic reassures General Baros in several ways. One is here where he points out that: "All right. You don't have to hurry. You have time. You have food down there. You have water, ammunition. Don't worry about anything." Sir, based on your knowledge, was it true that the soldiers there did have food, water, and ammunition so that they could hold out for some time?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: The Marsal Tito barracks did not have soldiers but cadets of the military high school. These were practically kids of 14, 15, 16, 17 years of age. They were minors and there was a group in the final years of the military academy.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: There were just guards who were actually soldiers --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: -- in the barracks. Of course, food was provided through UNPROFOR. UNPROFOR made it possible for us to receive food supplies because until the 10th or the 11th of May, I was the logistics deputy or assistant. So through UNPROFOR and the team of the General Staff that was conducting negotiations with the government and the presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina about the blockade and the units leaving the barracks, especially the cadets. So at --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: -- no point in time were we left without water --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: -- without food --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, it's now three times that Ms. Bibles tried to intervene, perhaps because you are moving away from the question. Could you please listen. Perhaps you may not have heard it because you are listening to the interpretation. Could you carefully listen now to the next question by Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And actually I'll move --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [via videolink] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could actually now go to page 2 in the B/C/S. And in the English we'll start at the bottom of page 1 and then turn to page 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, in this part of the conversation General Mladic says: "The entire town has been sealed off and the entire Muslim population. They can't touch you. I will put it to them today in no uncertain terms because if they dare touch a single hair on the head of any of our members or on the head of any member of our soldiers' families or anyone else who will not submit to them ..." --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we move to the next page in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Now we have it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And I'll pick up with:

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: "... or anyone else who will not submit to them, then that will be the end of them." Sir, in proximity in time with this phone call, did Mladic tell you what he intended for Sarajevo with this threat?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: As for this conversation and all the other conversations after the telephone or the microphone would be handed over, I did not listen or listen into General Mladic's conversations that he had with General Baros or anyone else. When he came here on the 10th of May, General Mladic came to, as he said when he was acquainted with the situation in Sarajevo and broader, that he together with the presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the president or the presidency of the Serbian republic, as it was called at the time, would resolve all problems peacefully. And I can tell you that --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir -- oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: -- I did listen to that conversation from my office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please, Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like now show you a document that reflects some of the negotiations involving the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could go to P321. We'll be looking for page 8 in both languages. And I would direct attention to number 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, as this comes up, I can tell you that we're looking at a 20 May 1992 UNPROFOR report of a meeting which included General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And I see the original is a little weak.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'll just say that General Mladic is described in this meeting that if a peaceful solution couldn't be found to the barracks --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Whoops. Oh, I'm sorry, it's the English that's week.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: That if a peaceful solution couldn't be found to the barracks --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: There we go.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: -- that he would use other methods and destroy half the city. Sir, we've now considered evidence of what General Mladic promised General Baros in terms of retaliation. And now we see a threat in a meeting with UNPROFOR. Isn't it true that you had the assets, I believe you called them, the heavy artillery, to do exactly as General Mladic had threatened on the 20th of May?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: I was not aware of that threat of Mladic's until now. I didn't attend the negotiations because the General Staff team was there that represented the Yugoslav Peoples' Army and that conducted the negotiations. Sometimes the commander of the military district was present as well and that was General Mladic at the time. He did not have enough assets, not even to destroy one single building never mind half of Sarajevo. However, he had a tendency to make threats with an empty rifle, as the saying goes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: And an empty rifle presents a threat to both the person that is being threatened and the person who is holding that rifle.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: All right, sir. I would now like to direct --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Actually, Your Honour, at this point a Rule 90(E) caution may be appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what your question will be, but if you consider --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I might.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- it to be appropriate, then I'll deal with it. But before we do so, Witness, did I understand you well that you said that General Mladic at the time did not have the assets to even destroy one building, is that -- one single building? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [via videolink] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then at the request of Ms. Bibles, Mr. Gagovic, I read the following Rule to you: "A witness may object to making any statement which might tend to incriminate the witness. The Chamber may, however, compel the witness to answer the question. Testimony compelled in this way shall not be used as evidence in a subsequent prosecution against the witness for any offence other than false testimony." I've read this Rule to you. It means that if a truthful answer to any of the upcoming questions of Ms. Bibles would be -- would tend to incriminate yourself, that you would then be in a position to address me and to ask whether you are under an obligation to answer that question. You may even say, "I don't want to answer that question because a truthful answer would tend to incriminate myself," and then the Chamber will give a ruling on that. Is that clear to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [via videolink] Yes, it's clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed, Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could go to 65 ter 31232, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And, sir, this is a communication between you and an individual whose last name is Vukota, V-u-k-o-t-a, from 16 May 1992. And, sir, while this is coming up, I'll ask whether the name Vukota was a JNA lieutenant who stayed in Bosnia after the JNA -- as the JNA departed?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Not Vukota. Vukovic is a PhD holder and a colonel of the Yugoslav Peoples' Army. He taught at the air force military academy in Rajlovac. I think he taught psychological or philosophy. I'm not sure. But it's one of those two subjects.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you. So would the --

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Would the name --

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: -- he came from the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina. He hailed from there and territorially he came from there.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: With -- by May -- or 16th of May 1992, do you know where he was located?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: On the 16th of May 1992, he was in Rajlovac. His family was there. He was with the territorial unit -- actually, it was still not the Army of Republika Srpska but still the Territorial Defence unit in Rajlovac. They were securing the Rajlovac area. And I think it was below the slopes of the Hum, above Pofalici, towards Rajlovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And, sir, in this conversation you're reported as -- or he -- excuse me. In response to your question as to whether he's resisting, he tells you that he is: "With all my strength I'm striking, but I've got no wheat." You respond with: "There is wheat, just tell me where I should cover you from." He responds with: "Strike with all your strength on those and you won't be wrong." And then there appears to be a discussion following this about locations. First in the context of this conversation, what did you mean by "wheat"?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Most probably it was about -- it referred to ammunition, rifle, machine-gun ammunition and so on. The conversation was conducted on the 16th of May when Muslim units from the Sarajevo area launched an attack on Rajlovac which had a Serb majority population. The Rajlovac Territorial Defence put up a resistance to the attacking forces. And then when I was informed about it, because that happened in my area of responsibility since I was representing the commander. So when I was informed about the attack, I asked whether they were putting up resistance to the attack and he said yes, but they didn't have enough resistance. And I said, you can't have a shortage of ammunition. You must have some. But you also have our support, because the attack was carried out during a signed cease-fire, which was signed on the 14th of May, if I'm not mistaken, between the Serb republic leadership, the Muslims, UNPROFOR, and representatives of the JNA general command.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, I'd -- I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I just first verify the following. Witness, you said you know someone by the name of Vukovic, not Vukota. Now in --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [via videolink] His last name was Vukovic and his first name was Vukota. Dr. Vukota Vukovic, colonel. He is the person that I spoke with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That answers all my questions in this respect. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, in -- and just by way of background I'll let you know that the Trial Chamber has heard evidence that there was intense action around Sarajevo, including shelling, around the 14th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, that would be, say, Witness Wilson and P320 at paragraph 40.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: But, sir, I want to move on. If we could go to the last page of this document, which reflects a second phone call between the two of you. You've been asked for more assistance in the second phone call. You obtain, it appears, the location details. And then you ask: "Has it so far been okay what was sent?" The answer is: "Great. Please do the elevation 695," is it Velesici butts, and that's my confusion about what the translation may be for this location, but going back to the quote: "In that part in the very populated area of residence, that should be stricken as heavy as possible, and this part above the creamery and further as well." Sir, the simple first question is whether you provided fire after this at elevation 695?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Artillery fire was of the barrage type and the firing was executed in agreement with the other side between the attackers and the defenders in order to prevent the attackers from breaking through and to get them to return to their positions. However, that area is not populated. There were no civilians there and there was nothing else there other than weaponry of the two warring parties.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, is -- sir --

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know the size of the forces but it was probably a unit that was working in close co-ordination with the units in Rajlovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I'll tender 31232.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar -- Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P6724, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, next --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'd ask that P2729 be brought to our screens.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And, sir, I'm directing your attention now, as this comes up, to a 12 May 1992 phone call from an individual named - is it Popadic? - from Ilidza? Do you know who that is?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was the commander of the Ilidza Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If you'll bear with us just a moment while we have the English translation placed on the screen. All right. Sir, towards the bottom of the page on the English translation, we see a request for targets that should be fired. It appears to be a request, again, for assistance. And the question is whether these targets may be too far away from you, and you ask where the targets are.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And, sir, do you see the discussion of the various locations that are requested? Behind the Coca-Cola.

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. This was a group that was more of a paramilitary Muslim group than a military group, and they had two mortars that were mounted on motor vehicles. They were constantly moving then they would stop in a certain place, and then they would fire mortar shells at the Ilidza neighbourhood. We were asked, as it was previously agreed, to neutralise the fire and any attempts at such attacks on the civilians population.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And did you respond to this request?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: I was obliged to respond, but we did not because they left those positions. Once they fired a couple of projectiles on Ilidza, then they moved. They went into the city.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you. So --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And we can -- well, I didn't have any further questions about this document, but I'll stop and see whether the Chamber has any. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have no questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And I'd now like to shift direction and ask a couple of questions in the general area of paragraph 36 of your statement where you discuss your relationship with other entities. First, would you agree that in April and May of 1992 you were in constant communication with the leadership of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: I was not in communication in April and on the 10th of May because it was not my role to maintain communications with any institution. In May, I was appointed representatives of the command of the 4th Corps for talks and negotiations with the opposing side with the leadership of the Serbian republic and the municipalities -- actually, crisis staffs, not municipalities, that had been formed in certain municipalities. Communications were maintained with those crisis staffs and then also with representatives of the Muslim Bosnian army and representatives of the Serbian side of the Territorial Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I also conducted negotiations with Fikret Abdic, who was appointed by the Bosnia and Herzegovina presidency to be a liaison with the Yugoslav Peoples' Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall testifying in Dragomir Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did testify.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Didn't you testify that you were in constant communication with the leadership of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: I definitely did not say that. I was not in constant communication with them. I could not have been. I assumed command on the 11th of May. Before that, there was another corps commander. I was simply a liaison with the presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina and it went through Fikret Abdic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Perhaps I've confused the dates. After the 10th of May, were you, and I'll change the term, were you in communication with the leadership of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Following the 10th of May, the only contact I had with the leadership of the Serbian republic took place when the president of RS, Dr. Radovan Karadzic, came to Lukavica. He offered that I assume the position of commander once the Sarajevo Romanija Corps was established. I thanked him for the offer.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not hear the end of the answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [via videolink] The Muslim side also made the same offer. They offered that I command the Bosnia-Herzegovina TO. I thanked them as well and I refused the offer. I told them I was a national of the FRY who was to return to his state. I told them that the problems they had were their own and that they should deal with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Sir, do you recall being asked about your communications with the leadership of Republika Srpska when you testified in the Dragomir Milosevic trial?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: I don't off the cuff, but do remind me --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: -- and then I might confirm or deny.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And the reference would be at transcript 8706. "Q. By 'leadership of Republika Srpska' who in particular are you referring to, sir? "A. Well, specifically, we were in communication with the President of Republika Srpska, Radovan Karadzic at the time." Does that refresh your recollection about this area testimony?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe it's been a standing procedure in this courtroom to have the transcript on the screen when it's being quoted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And, I'm sorry, Your Honour, I did not get this preloaded. I'll withdraw the question at this point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: This confirms what I stated but not the way my statement was interpreted. There was a communication link by phone like the one we are sharing now. It doesn't mean that we were in contact or that we made agreements as to what to do. We only used it in cases when their forces were engaging the JNA so as to exert influence. It wasn't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [via videolink] -- that there were convictions taking place but there was a phone line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles has withdrawn the question. Nevertheless the witness has started to answer it. I'm looking to you, Mr. Ivetic, what to do under the present circumstances? We can strike the answer because the question has been withdrawn. We also could receive the evidence if you consider it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, I think -- I think the witness did have his recollection refreshed, so in that sense it's okay. But in terms of context, if there are going to be additional questions relied on from this transcript, we would like to have the same privileges that were enjoyed by the Prosecution, that is, to have the documents on the screen so that we can view the context and see if there are any questions that arise from the direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So for the testimony from the witness until now, you say that although the question has been withdrawn, you do not insist on striking the answer. The testimony stands. If Ms. Bibles --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour. And I apologise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then for any future question in this context, you should show the relevant portion of the transcript. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, we could put the relevant portion of the transcript on the screen if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then if you have any further questions --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- then please do as instructed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I, before you continue, seek one clarification. Mr. Gagovic, some minutes ago you referred to Mr. Karadzic who came to Lukavica and offered you to assume the position of commander once the Sarajevo Romanija Corps was established. You thanked him for this offer, as you said, and what was the result of all of that? Did you accept it or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [via videolink] I did not accept. I think I clarified that. I'm not sure you understood. I thanked him for the offer and I suggested to him that he should pick another officer who was a BH national. I told him I was an FRY national. And following the lifting of the blockade of the barracks, my intention was to go back to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I -- the reason why I asked you was that when you gave your answer earlier, the interpreters didn't catch the end of your answer. But now you were referring to Mr. Karadzic's offer or the offer of the Muslim side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [via videolink] Both sides made an offer. One offer was made by President Karadzic and the other by the Muslim side. They offered that I act as the TO BH commander. Colonel Hasan Efendic was at that position at the time. I thanked them as well and refused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [via videolink] Giving the same explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [via videolink] I suggested that they should talk to the Serbian republic in order to reach a common understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that clarification.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, in paragraph 36 --

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: -- you indicate that you co-operated with various legal representatives including the Serbian MUP.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'd like to go to 65 ter 31231.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And, sir, this is an intercept of a phone call on the 14th of May, 1992, between yourself and Mico Stanisic. This is a very short intercept.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And I would ask that we play this. I recognise that we may have to play it twice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles, has a transcript been provided to the booth?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then you play it again so that we can receive translation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] MG: Yes. "NN: Hello. "MG: Yes. "NN: Good afternoon. "MG: Good afternoon. "NN: Communications centre of the Serbian ministry. "MG: What can I do for you, this is Colonel Gagovic. "NN: Just a second, the Minister wants to talk to you. "MS: Hello. "MG: Yes. "MS: Good afternoon. "MG: Good afternoon. "MS: This is Mico Stanisic. "MG: What can I do for you? "MS: Are you okay? "MG: Well, great. "MS: What's up at your place? "MG: Well, we are waging the war. "MS: Are you? "MG: Well, yes. "MS: Due to the confidentiality of the phone number I am going to -- I just wanted to tell you that I am here in Vrace. "MG: Yes. "MS: So you can call me if you need anything. "MG: All right. I have the phone number for Karlo. "MS: Great. "MG: All right. "MS: And this is Miler. "MG: All right. "MS: Write it down. "MG: Of course. "MS: That's a deal. "MG: Cheers. "MS: Have a nice day."

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, first, do you recognise your voice in that phone call?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: I suppose it's mine although I'm not 100 per cent certain. The tone of voice seems slightly off but it is possible that the conversation took place. Minister Stanisic probably called me once he reached the area of responsibility of the 4th Corps command.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise Mico Stanisic's voice in this phone call?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: No. I didn't speak to him often. I wouldn't be able to recognise his voice. Given the tone of the conversation and its seriousness, I suppose it could be him.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, he gives what appears to be a code-name, which is Miler. Is that the code-name that he would have used?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Do you --

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you mean if I used it as a pseudonym? No, no. I always introduced myself by my first, last name, as well as by rank no matter who I talked to.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Can you tell us who Karlo is?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, it was the police commander in Novo Sarajevo. Since there was some miscommunication in terms of the competence of JNA members and that of the police of the Serbian republic, we were in contact whenever there was a dispute, especially if it referred to traffic and other priorities.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, in this conversation you indicate, I believe: "Well, we are waging the war." And this is the 14th of May 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness please wait for the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [via videolink] [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness first wait for the question to be put to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, are you talking about the kind of activity that we've discussed on the 14th of May in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: No. It was simply the term that was under such wartime circumstances. We were waging a war and we were in a position to defend ourselves. It wasn't in the context of any further operations and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, I do have a question. Isn't it true that when it came to combat, periods of combat, the Serbian MUP was subordinated to your command?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAV GAGOVIC
utterances.text: No, the Serbian MUP was never under my command unless something had to be dealt with within the area of responsibility which was our competence. If they became involved, we intervened.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I would tender 31231.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I would, however, have a few additional questions. Witness, you were asked about the words spoken: "We are waging the war." You said, well, we were just in a war. That's all. Nothing special. Now, the question was: "What's up at your place?" Then apparently you said, "Well, we are waging the war." And is there any use on the 14th of May to tell your interlocutor that the war was ongoing? I mean, wasn't that common knowledge not worth of any question apart from if you wanted to know what exactly happened at the location referred to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [via videolink] He didn't know anything. He just came to Vrace. It was a part of Sarajevo that was not engaged. It was not controlled. The police was billeted in the former police high school of Bosnia-Herzegovina. When he arrived from Pale, he called. It was just a chitchat so to say, well, we're waging the war. By that time, we were engaged in intensive talks with the presidency and the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina in order to have the JNA barracks and members deblocked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ivetic is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have been directed to the B/C/S original for this intercept which does not correspond entirely to the "We are waging a war." In B/C/S is [Interpretation] "While the war is being waged, sort of."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. Ivetic, for taking us to the B/C/S original. Ms. Bibles, you tendered 31231. Mr. Registrar, approximate the number would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P6725, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And finally, if we could go to P3855 and we'll be looking at paragraph 7 which I believe is on page 3 in the English and page 2 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we're waiting for that to be brought to our screens, Ms. Bibles, you earlier referred in relation to I think the testimony of Mr. Wilson to P320, paragraph 40, referring to the 14th of May. I see a reference to the 14th of May in paragraph 41, not --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Oh.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- however in paragraph 40. Could you please verify whether --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so. And meanwhile, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, on the 15th of May 1992, Mico Stanisic issued an order for the Serbian MUP.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And that's the document which is hopefully coming up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, I -- it -- I just realised that that document may not be in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's confirmed from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'm sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, in this document Minister Stanisic orders that the Serbian MUP be subordinated: "While participating in combat operations, the units of the ministry shall be subordinated to the command of the armed forces. However, the ministry units shall be under the direct command of certain ministry officials." Sir, I put it to you that, in fact, rather than having a co-operative relationship with the Serbian MUP, when it came to combat the Serbian MUP in fact was subordinated to your command?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would object. It misstates the document. The document does not talk about combat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles, there is -- could you please quote, then, from the document, exactly the portion --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour. The whole --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The whole of item number 7 should be read to have the context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could we nevertheless have it on our screens so that we could follow the reading even the if the witness is unable to follow the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And, sir, I'll read this slowly. "The use of the ministry units in co-ordinated action" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not on our screens yet --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
